explanation: Comb-like plates inside the bent bill sieve out algae and tiny shrimp. Pigments in that food are what turn flamingos pink: their chicks hatch grey or white.

claims.text: Flamingos feed with their heads upside down, filtering food from the water with their bills.
Roseate spoonbills, scarlet ibises and pink-backed pelicans do not filter-feed with their heads upside down.
Flamingo bills have comb-like plates that strain algae and small crustaceans from the water.
Flamingos get their pink colour from carotenoid pigments in their food.
Flamingo chicks hatch with grey or white down.
